summary: Agent gates can create an expensive illusion of independent assurance when they share models, context and blind spots, and blocking errors can overwhelm delivery.

points.text: Several named agents backed by the same model family and prompt corpus produce correlated judgments, so consensus is not equivalent to independent evidence.
False rejections accumulate across serial gates: even individually acceptable error rates can make the overall pipeline reject a large share of correct changes.
Agents may optimize visible criteria while missing integration, operational and organizational risks that are absent from their context window.
Gate latency, model cost and noisy remediation loops can exceed the value of reviewing low-risk changes unless checks are risk-tiered and cached.
